title: “Stupid Simple” Apps Are Making Millions While You Overthink

idea.name: The Data Supplier: packaged industry contact lists
idea.one_liner: Buy/aggregate industry contact lists (realtors, dentists, loan officers), package by industry and resell the same digital file repeatedly via SEO and cold email

key_quotes.quote: We're going to buy a bunch of others, and we're going to package these based on industry, and we're going to sell these lists.

and they were doing I think I want to say like $10,000 a month in revenue, something like that.

Every realtor in the US, 500 bucks. You want California list, it's 200 bucks." Some just bulk list.
We started ranking number one in no time from our on the borderline greyhat SEO at the time, and then we were cold emailing people.

acquisition_channels.details: ranked #1 for 'realtor email lists' etc. (grey hat)

ideas.delivery: Upload digital CSV, send link; Philippines call centre samples 500 numbers to verify accuracy

uk_legal_risk.reason: Reselling personal contact data (incl. sole-trader realtors and consumers) without lawful basis breaches UK GDPR; buyers using it for cold SMS/email to individuals breach PECR

stated_problem.quote: Still had some Fortune 500s, but a lot of them were small and medium-sized. They needed a clean list of their ideal prospects.
stated_problem.speaker: Will Cannon

idea.name: B2B custom data/lead-gen agency
idea.one_liner: Build custom, appended and verified prospect lists for SMBs, manually manipulating CSVs, plus some cold email and calling

key_quotes.quote: And yeah, that led to that kind of 10-year run-ish of being kind of self-employed and kind of just selling B2B data and doing kind of cold email and cold calling stuff.

claims.claim: High six to low seven figures profit/year
claims.quote: Some years are better than others, but it was probably high six, low seven figures.

uk_legal_risk.reason: Processing/reselling personal data needs UK GDPR lawful basis; sole-trader contacts covered by PECR

idea.name: Per-lead data sales business
idea.one_liner: Sell leads priced per lead (from ~50 cents) by quantity and type, alongside a bulk-list sister business

key_quotes.quote: So, she had her own business that was selling on a per cents model, per cents per lead, depending on quantity and type and everything else.

stated_problem.quote: And the whole time you're thinking, "This needs to be automated. This needs to be a SaaS." But it's hard.
stated_problem.speaker: Chris Koerner

idea.name: UpLead B2B sales leads SaaS
idea.one_liner: Self-serve B2B contact data platform (ZoomInfo competitor) built by an Upwork dev team, grown via cold email using its own data

key_quotes.quote: And we got our first customers through cold email. We were using our tool to build out lists of people.

claims.quote: I think it was like 2,000 a month, 5,000 a month, 8,000 a month, 10,000 a month.
I think within the first year, we were probably doing a million ARR first year.

acquisition_channels.details: script with multiple follow-ups, dogfooding own data

ideas.delivery: Outsourced dev team from Upwork; husband-and-wife team then hires

uk_legal_risk.reason: B2B contact data includes personal data of named individuals — UK GDPR legitimate-interest and transparency obligations

1% of documents, all documents worldwide that are signed are electronically signed.

stated_problem.quote: Let's say today that dentist is paying 300 a month for HubSpot.
stated_problem.speaker: Chris Koerner

idea.name: Free vertical CRM monetized by payment processing
idea.one_liner: Give a niche CRM (e.g. for dentists) away free via GoHighLevel sub-accounts, requiring clients to move card processing to a white-labelled processor on interchange-plus, plus payroll/insurance upsells
idea.offer: free industry CRM bundled with payments
idea.revenue_model: payment processing residuals (~1% of volume) plus ancillary services

key_quotes.quote: This is a free CRM for dentists and I'm making it for whatever industry and I'm making it the best CRM possible for that very specific niche vertical.
You have a three to $500 a month agency account, and you can have unlimited sub accounts for free.

claims.quote: you're making $1,000 a month from this client that like their CRM is now free, their credit card fees didn't go up at all
And so you're making three and a half times what HubSpot was making for the same thing, but it's a win-win-win all the way around.

claims.claim: Ancillary services often more profitable than software
claims.quote: a lot of times those other ancillary services around the software are sometimes a lot more profitable than the software itself, right?

ideas.delivery: GoHighLevel white-label sub-accounts plus white-label card processor
ideas.other_uk_rules: Payment ISO/agent arrangements; FCA rules sit with processor

idea.name: Squire all-in-one barbershop software
idea.one_liner: Vertical all-in-one software for barber shops bundling payments, payroll, insurance

key_quotes.quote: They have like I think it's a CRM for barber shops. They have like all-in-one tool for barber shops.

idea.name: FSBO scrape-and-bulk-text cash offers
idea.one_liner: Scrape Zillow FSBO listings daily, bulk text owners a cash offer ~40% below Zestimate via custom Twilio software

key_quotes.quote: I paid a guy on Upwork one or two thousand bucks to build my own custom bulk texting software built on Twilio.

claims.quote: I can close fast, all cash, 60,000 today." And 98% say screw you or no, and 2% are like, let's talk, you know?
We ended up buying a few houses in other states that we never saw in person and we completely lost our shirts

uk_legal_risk.reason: Unsolicited bulk SMS to individual homeowners is banned under PECR; scraping personal numbers breaches UK GDPR

idea.name: Done-for-you cold email agency
idea.one_liner: Agency running outbound cold email (servers, deliverability) for clients

key_quotes.quote: I have some friends now that do done-for-you cold email, and it's like, you know, if you do it right, and you're and you're on top of your game

uk_legal_risk.reason: B2B cold email to corporate subscribers allowed under PECR with opt-out; not to sole traders
